findings.title: A merge for a funding or a Send now takes every mixed box before a larger box of another kind, so it can spend twice as many boxes together as the payment needs
findings.scenario:
1. A 1.9.1 user holds two ways back of the classic pool's 10 ₳ boxes, which 1.8.0's retired pools' run brought back: `box:<tx>`, origin lovejoin, about 9.7 ₳ each (L1, L2).
2. After this release, four boxes from the 5 ₳ pool come back by themselves, each marked mixed, about 4.7 ₳ each (M1 to M4).
3. The user funds a private session with 10 ₳, which is 15 ₳ out with its 5 ₳ collateral. No single UTxO pays, and each box is a class of its own, so steps 1 and 2 find nothing and merging starts with order a.
4. by_history sorts tier 2 by rank before size (Fund: Mixed 2, Lovejoin 3). It grows M1, M2 and M3 (14.1 ₳, still at or under the floor, so Skipped), then adds M4: four boxes spent together.
5. Before round four, Fund and Pay tied the two (`Lovejoin | Mixed`), and the same order grew L1, then L2: two boxes.
6. Order c, which spends as few boxes as pay, runs only after a. When the balance holds nothing but boxes it is never tried at all. The review's note says four boxes go together, and nothing says two would do. The two extra Seedelf inputs also add their share of the fee.

A 12 ₳ Send (Pay: Mixed 4, Lovejoin 5) works the same way: three or four mixed boxes where L1 and L2 paid. Payments in parts use the same order (Worth::apart sorts by tier, then rank, then size), so a large Send or funding spends every mixed box before a larger box of another kind. Mint has merged this way since B15 (Mixed 0, Lovejoin 2), but a stealth mint rarely needs two boxes.
findings.who: Nobody acts. It hits any user whose private balance holds boxes of two sizes, on an ordinary funding, top-up, Send or Make public that has to merge. Examples: a 1.9.1 way back from the classic 10 ₳ pool beside the 5 ₳ pool's, or a merged way back that a private-paid escape hatch left (`box:X+box:P`, origin lovejoin, about twice the size).

findings.fix:
Put the box count first and the rank second, in order a and in Worth::apart's tier 2. Take the fewest boxes that pay after the rest (largest first, as a took them before round four), and among that many, take mixed ones first.
One way: add boxes by (rank, Reverse(lovelace)), but skip a box when the boxes left, largest first, can't close the gap within the count that largest-first needs; otherwise take the largest left.
Step 1's one-box order (l3rank#3) stays as it is.
A narrower alternative: when merging, put only a box with an `unknown:` part (unplacedBox) after the others, and keep mixed, plain and merged boxes largest first.
Test (apart_test.rs, or mint_test.rs mod apart): four mixed 4.7 ₳ ways back and two `box:<tx>` lovejoin ones of 9.7 ₳. A 15 ₳ funding (Fund { session: None }) and a 12 ₳ Send (Pay) each spend 2 boxes, one of them mixed where that pays at the same count. l3rank#3's one-box test still passes. The extension sees the change only after a WebAssembly rebuild.
findings.owner_question: When a spend must merge boxes, should it spend as few boxes as pay, taking a mixed one first only among that many, or take mixed boxes first even where that merges more of them?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 1e1b0647. I traced it from the extension to core and found no guard the finder missed. It reproduces exactly, and the same test passes with round three's build.rs.

1. How the boxes are classed
- The finder's L1 and L2 are 1.9.1 ways back. activity.ts:819-820 `case "lovejoin-withdraw": return boxFrom(entry.txHash);` gives `box:<tx>`, origin lovejoin.
- A new way back that a mix made gets `mixedBox` (`box:<tx>`, origin mixed) at lovejoin.ts:8230-8236.
- lib.rs:2158-2159 maps "lovejoin" to Origin::Lovejoin and "mixed" to Origin::Mixed.

2. Nothing on the way reorders or holds back a box
- readContract (script-spend.ts:239-246) passes every free UTxO with its class.
- buildFunding (sessions.ts:3164-3182) builds `{ utxos, payments, classes, funding }`.
- build_withdraw_parts tries one transaction first (lib.rs:5155-5156 `match build_withdraw(sk, request.clone()) { Ok(one) => return Ok(vec![one])`).
- withdraw_spend (lib.rs:3827-3841) calls `build::sweep_many_apart` with `Purpose::Fund` for a funding or top-up and Pay for a Make public. A Send goes through transfer_spend (lib.rs:3395-3399), `transfer_apart` with `Purpose::Pay`.

3. In core
- `apart` is reached at build.rs:2716-2717.
- Step 1 skips every single box: :2837 `if lovelace <= u128::from(floor) ... return Tried::Skipped;`, with floor = paid_out (:3629, :3334).
- Step 2 finds no class with two rows, since each box is a class of its own.
- Step 3, order a, sorts by :2936-2945 `(last(u), tier(u), !joins_base(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)), holds_tokens(u), std::cmp::Reverse(lovelace_of(u)))`. The rank comes before the size. Fund ranks `Mixed => 2, Lovejoin => 3` (:2529-2530) and Pay `Mixed => 4, Lovejoin => 5` (:2505-2506).
- grow returns on the first build (:2800-2806), and order a runs first (:3002).
- Order c, the fewest boxes, is filtered out when the balance holds only boxes: :2987-2988 `.filter(|_| !largest.is_empty())`.

4. The run (mint_test, mod apart)
- The balance: four mixed boxes of 4.71 ₳ and two plain `box:<tx>` lovejoin boxes of 9.71 ₳.
- On HEAD:
  - a funding of 10 ₳ plus its 5 ₳ collateral spent 4 mixed boxes, fee 377,032, where 2 plain boxes pay at fee 285,818;
  - a site's top-up of 15 ₳: 4 boxes against 2;
  - a Make public and a Send of 12 ₳: 3 mixed boxes against 2, 45,608 lovelace more fee each.
- With 51e66221's build.rs swapped into the copy, all four spent 2 boxes. That is a regression from round three.
- No existing test merges mixed boxes with other boxes of different sizes. The l3rank#3 pins cover one box only.

5. Comments and docs
- build.rs:2986 `// With nothing but boxes, a grew these already.` is stale: order a's box order is no longer c's.
- architecture.md:141's "So it spends as few boxes as pay" is true of order 3 only, which runs after orders 1 and 2 fail.
- privacy.md:173 and flows.md:377 do say that merging takes a mixed box before any other. The docs match the code, but nothing says a merge can spend more boxes than pay.
- The R4-code fixer avoided exactly this in c ("ranking there could merge two boxes where one pays"), but the rank went into order a, which runs first.

6. Severity: medium, as the finder rated it
- The user can't turn it off: 1 or 2 more box histories are merged on an ordinary funding, top-up, Send or Make public.
- The fee overpaid is 45,608 to 91,214 lovelace, with no warning.
- For the finder's own examples, a 1.9.1 plain `box:<tx>` and a `box:X+box:P` merge, histories.ts `knownBox` already counts the box as one whose making the wallet knows. The extra merges buy nothing by the lead's own criterion for the escape hatch.
- The case for low: on mainnet it needs larger non-mixed boxes (the classic pool's 10 ₳ ways back, or a box-paid hatch merge), a dwindling legacy set.
- It is a real trade-off for a larger box of unknown making (`box:<w>+unknown:<w>`). In case 1 the only 2-box set that pays is both plain boxes, so putting the count first means spending boxes the l3rank#3 rule ranks after mixed ones. That is the owner's question as the finder put it.
- Not tested: Worth::apart (lib.rs:4134-4142) puts the rank before the total in tier 2 too. The consequence for parts is inferred from that sort key.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Ask the owner the finder's question first. If the answer is to spend as few boxes as pay and take mixed ones first among that many, this is a fix I prototyped in the copy. The whole seedelf-core suite passed with it: every binary ok, mint_test 61 (both new tests included), apart_test 17, merge_test 6, selection_integration 8, proptest_core 8.

1. build.rs:2936-2945 (order a)
- Drop the rank in tier 2, so the boxes go largest first, as in round three. Bind `let t = tier(u);` and use `if t == 2 { 0 } else { purpose.rank(&class(u)) }` where the key has `purpose.rank(&class(u))`.
- The rank still orders tiers 0 and 1.
- Step 1 (`one_more`, l3rank#3's one-box rule) is untouched.

2. grow (:2795-2808)
- Have it report the prefix length it built with, for example `Grown::Built(T, usize)`.

3. In the orders loop (:3006-3016)
- When order a (the first) builds with `order[..k]`, count its pure-ADA boxes: j in all, `had` of them at the best box rank (the minimum `purpose.rank` among `boxes`, which is Mixed for every purpose).
- Split `boxes` (:2957-2958, already sorted largest first) into `firsts` at that rank and `others`.
- For kk from min(j, firsts.len()) down to had+1, skipping any kk where j−kk > others.len(), try a's non-box inputs (order[..k] without the boxes) plus `firsts[..kk]` plus `others[..j-kk]`, through `try_with`.
- Return the first that builds, or else a's own build.
- These are extra tries after a has already built, so nothing new is ever refused. There are at most j of them, and those under the floor are skipped for free.
- Mint changes the same way. It rarely needs two boxes.

4. Words
- Fix build.rs:2986's comment, and the step 3 doc of select_script_inputs (:2664-2674).
- architecture.md:140-141: order 1 takes the fewest boxes that pay, mixed ones first among that many.
- privacy.md:173 and flows.md:377: "as few boxes as pay, one the wallet knows is mixed first among them".

5. WebAssembly
- Worth::apart's tier 2 (lib.rs:4134-4142) should get the same treatment, or at least the total before the rank in tier 2. That's untested; parts only run when one transaction can't take the payment.
- The extension sees any core change only after a WebAssembly rebuild.

6. A narrower option, if the owner wants a mixed box first even at a higher count
- Rank only a box with an `unknown:` part (unplacedBox) after the others, and keep mixed, plain and merged boxes largest first, matching `knownBox`.
- That needs a rank by class parts in `Purpose::rank`.

7. Pins to add
- The two tests in the test field below.
- The same-count pin passes on HEAD too. It guards the l3rank#3 rule in merging under either fix.

verdicts.evidence:
The mechanism holds as described. I couldn't refute it on the code. But the impact is smaller than medium, and the behaviour follows the rule round four was asked to build.

TRACE (tree at 1e1b0647)
1. Each way back is a class of its own.
   - histories.ts:66: `boxFrom = (txHash) => ({ id: `box:${txHash}`, origin: "lovejoin" })`, one per withdraw.
   - activity.ts:820: a 1.9.1 or 1.8.0 withdraw entry kept with no origin reads `boxFrom(entry.txHash)`. So a retired-run classic way back is a plain `box:<tx>`, origin lovejoin.
   - lovejoin.ts:632: `LOVEJOIN_DENOM = 10_000_000n`. mint_test.rs:2799: `BOX = 9_710_000` ("10 ₳ less the withdraw's fee"), so a 5 ₳ box comes back at about 4.71 ₳.
2. A funding reaches core's order.
   - sessions.ts:2033-2046 pays the amount plus `SESSION_COLLATERAL`, so 10 ₳ is 15 ₳ out.
   - lib.rs:5155-5156: build_withdraw_parts tries one transaction first.
   - lib.rs:3828-3841: withdraw_spend sends `Purpose::Fund` through `sweep_many_apart`; a Send and Make public send Pay.
   - build.rs:3629: floor = `paid_out`.
3. Steps 1 and 2 don't pay.
   - Every single is Skipped: build.rs:2837 `if lovelace <= u128::from(floor) … Tried::Skipped`.
   - Step 2 has nothing to try: every class holds one row (:2888 `for k in 2..`).
4. Order a picks by rank first.
   - Ranks: build.rs:2527-2535 Fund `Mixed => 2, Lovejoin => 3`; :2500-2507 Pay `Mixed => 4, Lovejoin => 5`. Both were `Lovejoin | Mixed` before 5709e0c1. :2546 gives both tier 2.
   - :2936-2945 `(last, tier, !joins_base, purpose.rank, holds_tokens, Reverse(lovelace))`: rank before size.
   - grow (:2800-2806) returns at the first build, and a runs first (:3002).
5. Worked numbers.
   - 15 ₳ funding: M1..M3 is 14.13 (Skipped); M1..M4 is 18.84, leaving 3.84 for fee and change, so 4 boxes. Before round four: L1 9.71 (Skipped), then L1+L2 19.42, so 2 boxes.
   - 12 ₳ Send: three mixed boxes (14.13), where L1+M1 (14.42) or L1+L2 would pay with two.
6. Order c doesn't rescue it.
   - :2987-2988 `filter(|_| !largest.is_empty())` drops c when the balance holds only boxes.
   - Even when c runs, it comes after a.
7. Payments in parts do the same: lib.rs:4134-4142 sorts `(tier, !(alone||own), rank, Reverse(total), id)`.

BEYOND THE FINDING
- With tokens sent, boxes are never singles (:2866) and never the "one more" (:2904 tier 0 only). The same happens with tier-0 money short by one box. In both cases a merges two or more mixed boxes where the base plus one larger plain box pays.
  - Example: Unknown 3 ₳, 4×4.71 mixed and 9.71 plain, an 11 ₳ Make public. a spends U+M1+M2+M3. Before round four it spent U+L, or U+L+M1.
  - So the section comment build.rs:2664-2667 ("so two are spent together only when nothing else pays") is now false for Fund and Pay. It has been false for Mint since B15.
- :2986 "With nothing but boxes, a grew these already" is stale. It is harmless: b (:2946-2955) is now that size-first order.
- Rank also comes before holds_tokens, so a mixed token box goes ahead of a plain ADA box.

IMPACT
- Who: nobody acts. It needs a user whose non-mixed boxes are larger than their mixed ones, such as 1.8.0's retired-run classic ways back (9.71 ₳) or a hatch-paid way back merged with another box (`box:P+box:X`, about twice the size). It also needs a funding, top-up, Send or Make public that no single UTxO or class pays. Two boxes of the same size (5 ₳ pool, 1.9.1-era vs mixed) cost nothing extra.
- Money lost: about 0.036 ₳ per extra Seedelf input.
  - Execution: the measured 76,043 mem and 337.8M steps (build.rs:1186-1192) at mainnet's 0.0577 and 0.0000721 come to about 0.029 ₳.
  - Size: an input and its redeemer, about 170 B at 44 lovelace/B, are about 0.007 ₳.
  - That is about 0.07 ₳ in the example.
- Privacy: more of the user's mixed boxes are linked in one transaction. The code's own model says this undoes mixing, and more boxes give a sharper intersection with a deposit. But count-first links boxes the wallet can't place: a 1.9.1-era `box:<tx>` may be a planted box, or an unmixed deposit's box (a session's). That is what the rule avoids.
  - The policy says so as written (privacy-policy.md:93): "A session's funding or a private payment, too, takes a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of."
  - review3.json l3rank#3's fix (A) named merge order a as covered. So this was intended in direction. Only its box count was never put to the owner: that question was asked about one box.
- What catches it: nothing in code. The review's note names each box merged, but not that fewer would pay. A user can lock boxes on the UTxOs screen (coin-control.ts:309, seedelf `u.locked`).
- Docs aren't wider than the code:
  - architecture.md:139 gives order 1 as "then the purpose's rank … the largest first".
  - :141's "So it spends as few boxes as pay" describes order 3.
  - flows.md:377 gives fewest boxes only as the fallback.
  - privacy.md:173 says a mixed box comes before any other.

SEVERITY: low, down from medium. It is a small cost in an edge case, and a trade-off made in the direction of the stated rule and the policy. The owner's question is genuine.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 1e1b0647. I traced it end to end and found no guard the finder missed. A Vitest run with the real WebAssembly reproduces it. 1. The payer order. lovejoin.ts:8146 `const fromLovejoin = (u: KoiosUtxo) => (knownBox(classes[outpoint(u)]) ? 0 : 1);` and :8150-8151 sort by fromLovejoin, then `another`, then the smaller. histories.ts:219-220 `c?.origin === "mixed" || (c?.origin === "lovejoin" && parts(c).every((p) => p.startsWith("box:")))` gives true both for X = {box:, mixed} and for P = {box:

, lovejoin}. `another` (:8149) reads only public: parts, so it is 0 for both. The size decides. 2. Nothing re-sorts or filters on the way. readContract (script-spend.ts:220-247) drops only reserved and locked rows, and classesOf (:276-277) drops only the bare "unknown". wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:2951-3010 withdraw_private_in walks `for utxo in &request.utxos` and returns the first that builds. Both ways in pass "private": the question's default, and Bring every box back now's stuck path (lovejoin.ts:7904 `...(stuck ? { paid: "private" as const } : {})`). 3. P is real upgrade data. At web-wallet/1.9.1 (f265d178), withdrawOne :7665 has `origin = spent ? merged([...]) : undefined`. Its settle :7852 has `isHistoryClass(w.origin) ? { origin: w.origin } : tiedOrigin(w.txHash, ties)`, and tiedOrigin gives {} when nothing is tied. 1.9.1's depositAccountOf returns undefined for a session's chain or entry and for a stranger's deposit. So a session's unmixed seed, or Mallory's box, that paid its own way back kept no origin. - HEAD's activity.ts classOf (:807-820) reads such an entry as boxFrom(tx). - entrySession (rpc.ts:153) applies only to session-out and session-back, so historiesByTx never merges it into a session. - Nothing rewrites kept entries: the only `entry.origin =` is in sent() (activity.ts:443). - A 1.9.1 withdraw still in flight at the update settles the same way. 4. On HEAD, only an ownMixOf way back that pays for itself is plain. lovejoin.ts:8230-8236 has `deposited !== undefined || ownMixOf(s, box) ? boxFrom(...)`, but a deposited box gets public: through `besides`, so its origin is "own". findings.title: When a page leaves its connect question or its unlock wait while another tab of the same site waits for the unlock to sign, the site never has to wait, though the policy says it does
findings.scenario:
Case 1, a connect question left:
1. Site X's tab A asks to connect, and the wallet locks while the question waits.
2. Tab B calls signData with an API object kept from before. That is an unlock wait, not an enable().
3. A reloads. gone(A) finds B in `unlocking`, so sharedBeyond is true, and it marks X spared with `question`.
4. A's enable() then ends. countEnabling finds no other enable() of X and deletes the mark at once (:620-623).
5. Nothing ever lands the decline, and A's reload can ask again with no wait.

Case 2, an unlock wait left:
1. Tab A's signTx and tab B's signTx both wait for the unlock.
2. A reloads, and X is marked spared without `question`.
3. Since round four the unlock clears that mark (:795), so no wait ever follows here either.

What the docs say: the policy's dApps row (privacy-policy.md:29) and its 18 November entry (:93) say such a site has to wait "unless another of its pages is asking to connect too", but B is asking to sign. architecture.md:563, as R4-docs wrote it, says "a connect question left stays owed", which case 1 doesn't keep.
Cost: only the site's own back-off. A site can dodge it by keeping any call waiting for the unlock in another tab, and for a connected site a refusal is nearly invisible anyway.
findings.who: A site with two tabs, with ordinary timing or on purpose: one tab keeps a signature waiting for the unlock while the other reloads past its connect question or its unlock wait.
findings.evidence:
dapp.ts:985-990 sharedBeyond: `[...(this.enabling.get(session.origin)?.keys() ?? [])].some(live) || this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin)`, which counts any method.
dapp.ts:620-623 countEnabling: `this.enabling.delete(session.origin); … this.spared.delete(session.origin);`.
dapp.ts:792-797 stateChanged: `if (!this.spared.get(u.session.origin)?.question) this.spared.delete(u.session.origin);`.
privacy-policy.md:29: "or whose page goes away before you answer its question (a reload, say, unless another of its pages is asking to connect too), has to wait". :93 says the same, and so do privacy.md:350 and flows.md:436.
round4.json R4-code policy_facts: "naming it is a wording call", which 8b36053d didn't take up.
findings.fix:
Option (a): count only an enable()'s unlock wait as sparing the site, `this.unlocking.some((u) => u.enable && u.session.origin === session.origin)` at dapp.ts:989. A page leaving beside a signature's wait is then declined at once, as the policy reads. A connected site's later signatures then meet the 10 s refusal only if the wallet locks again within it. This reverses dapp-gone's first new l3still#4 case.
Option (b): keep the code and say what it does. Add "or waiting for the unlock" to the policy's row and entry, privacy.md:350 and flows.md:436, and have architecture.md:563 say that a question left beside only a signature's wait isn't owed.
Test (dapp-gone): with the wallet locked and a connect question waiting, tab B's signData waits and tab A leaves its question. Under (a), expect declined() to list X.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 1e1b0647 (5709e0c1, 8b36053d, 1e1b0647). I traced it end to end and ran a test in a copy, now deleted. The fixes tree is clean.

**Case 1: a connect question left while another page's signature waits for the unlock**
- Any https page can do this. No API object kept from before is needed.
  - bridge.ts:89-97 `relay` forwards any `isDappMethod`.
  - sw.ts:408-421 passes it through `answerSite` (dapp.ts:3025-3039) to `dapp.call` with no enable() gate.
- A lock leaves a connect question waiting: stateChanged returns for "locked" (dapp.ts:791).
- B's signData while locked goes run() → unlocked() (:633-638) and is pushed to `unlocking` with `enable` false (:1665-1673). It is never counted in `enabling` (:593 counts enable() only).
- gone(A) (:949-979) finds the question (:959). `sharedBeyond` is true only through `this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin)` (:989). So the mark is set with `question: true` (:966-970) instead of refuseFor (:964).
- gone() rejects the question (:973-976), so A's enable() ends. call()'s finally (:608) runs countEnabling, which finds no other enable() and runs `this.enabling.delete(session.origin); … this.spared.delete(session.origin);` (:620-623).
- The test's diagnostic: right after gone(asks) the mark is `{"title":"Example","network":"preprod","question":true}`; once A's enable() has ended it is `null`.

**No guard lands the decline later**
- stateChanged's clear (:795) finds no mark.
- sparedNoMore lands only for a page in `enabling` (:1002), which B never is.
- A reload's enable() only clears marks (:1675, :1727).
- Only B leaving before the unlock (gone(B) → refuseFor) or the user closing the window (:853-856) turns the site away, and those are declines for B's own wait.
- On the ordinary path the user unlocks and B hears NOT_CONNECTED. declined() is then [] and a reload's page is asked.

**Case 2: an unlock wait left beside another page's signature wait**
- gone(a) sets the mark without `question`: `{"title":"Example","network":"preprod"}`.
- While still locked, a reload's enable() is asked and clears the mark itself (:1675). Otherwise the unlock clears it (:795; `null` after the unlock).
- This is l3still#4's design, pinned by dapp-gone.test.ts:620-638.

**Reload loop**
- While one signData waits for the unlock, five reloads in an enable()'s unlock wait each call window.show() (:1677), which focuses the window with drawAttention (dapp-window.ts:24). Result: "window shown" five times.
- In the control, with nothing else waiting, the next page is refused instead.

**What the docs say**
- privacy-policy.md:29 and :93 say "unless another of its pages is asking to connect too". privacy.md:350 says such sites "are kept in session storage". flows.md:436 says the same for a connect question. B is asking to sign, not to connect.
- architecture.md:563's "a connect question left stays owed" is false for case 1.
- Its reason for the unlock clause, "which asks itself and a refusal would turn away", is false for a signature. Only enable() (:1215) and unlocked() (:1658) read `refusing`. After the unlock, a waiting signature goes on to site() and ask() with no refusal check (:640-679, :1700-1703).
- Under option (a), the l3still#4 case shows this: B's signature was still asked after X was refused.
- The owner's B7 (DECISIONS.md:352) reads "except when another page of the same site waits on that question".
- Round three's verdict and R4-code's policy_facts both left the wording as an open call, and 8b36053d didn't change it.

**Severity: low, as the finder rated it**
- The policy promises more than the code, but what it over-promises is the site's own back-off and a refusal record that is never written. Nothing more is sent or revealed.
- It needs a lock while a question waits plus another tab's signature or send (case 1), or two signature waits (case 2).
- B7's exception already lets a site skip the back-off with two enable() tabs, so this gives a site no new reach.
- For a connected site a refusal is nearly invisible:
  - declined() leaves it out (:1333).
  - Its enable() returns before the refusal check (:1186-1190).
  - Only its signatures made while locked, within the wait, are refused (:1658-1660).

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 1e1b0647, but its numbers are wrong. I traced the path from the worker to core and found no guard the finder missed. A failing test shows it: a Send, a Make public and a funding all spend W when X would pay with the same inputs.

The finding's own numbers don't reproduce:
- A Seedelf UTxO holds at least 1,456,780 lovelace on the test parameters, so 14 UTxOs of 1 ₳ can't exist.
- Selection's estimate allows 22 Seedelf inputs, so 14 small UTxOs fit in one transaction. Step 2 pays 9 ₳ from the Own class with no box at all.
- The corrected trigger: at least 23 tier-0 UTxOs (money that isn't a box), where the largest 22 can't pay but one box plus 21 of them can.

The path:
1. Classes.
   - histories.ts:84 `unplacedBox = merged([boxFrom(txHash), unknownIn(txHash)])`. REACH (:144) puts lovejoin first, so W's origin is lovejoin.
   - mixedBox (:75) gives origin mixed. madePrivate (:64) gives `public:<n>`, own.
   - wasm lib.rs:2145-2171 maps these to Origin::Lovejoin, Mixed and Own.
2. What the worker sends.
   - readContract (script-spend.ts:220-247) sends every free UTxO with its class. Only the user's own locks are taken out (coin-control.ts:290-293).
   - transfer.ts:92-104 adds no filter.
   - build_transfer_parts (lib.rs:5011) and build_withdraw_parts (:5155) try one transaction first and return it when it builds.
3. Core.
   - transfer_apart and sweep_many_apart go to apart. Each attempt is paying plus estimate().
   - estimate() guesses 450M steps per input (build.rs:1189-1192) against MAX_TX_BUDGET's 10B (:1181-1184). Past 22 inputs, settle (:2085-2087) returns TooMany, which counts as Tried::Failed.
   - Step 2 and merge order a (:2935-2945, tier then rank) put every box after all tier-0 money. With 23 or more of those UTxOs, step 2 breaks at TooMany, and orders a and b fail at 23 before reaching any box.
   - Order c sorts boxes by `(!joins_base(u), std::cmp::Reverse(lovelace_of(u)))` (:2957-2958), and fewest_boxes takes `boxes[..j]` (:2987-2993). So j = 1 is the largest box.
   - Ranks are used only at :2865, :2884 and :2941.
   - Order b (:2946-2955) and order d (:2994-2995) also sort by size. But b can't reach a box after a fails, because it takes the same tier-0 rows first. Order c is the reachable one.
4. The review: historiesNote shows the same note for either box ("a box back from Lovejoin and money you made private together"). There is no choice, and Send goes as it is.

The harm: Mallory follows her box C to its withdraw and on to W. Spending W ties S1 to the Send's other inputs (money made private from account 0, so the public account) and to its recipient. X ties nothing.

The docs claim otherwise:
- Policy :93: "A session's funding or a private payment, too, takes a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of."
- architecture.md:137: "(l3rank#3: no box someone else put in is picked over a mixed one on size)". This contradicts its own :141, "the j largest boxes".
- privacy.md:173 says the same without any qualifier.
- flows.md:377 gives the rule, then "spending as few boxes as pay" without saying the largest goes first.
- Code comments say the same: build.rs:2471-2472, :2484-2488, :2497-2499, and the histories.ts header :22-24.

R4-code knew about order c and left it (round4.json "left": "merge order c ... still orders boxes by size alone, for every purpose, Mint included").

On severity: the rubric's letter puts "a claim wider than the code" at medium. I kept low because it needs a planted box, the user's Bring every box back now, 23 or more small UTxOs, and W larger than X (a coin flip on withdraw fees). That matches how l3rank#3 and l3docs#3 were rated. The lead may raise it.

findings.title: The policy's exception for a page that leaves ('unless another of its pages is asking to connect too') is narrower than the code. Since round four, another page waiting for the unlock spares the site for good
findings.scenario:
1. A connected site is open in two tabs and the wallet locks.
2. Both tabs call signTx, and each call waits for the unlock.
3. Tab A reloads. gone(A): its unlock wait is left, and sharedBeyond is true because tab B waits for the unlock. The site is spared with no `question`, and refuseFor doesn't run.
4. The user unlocks. B's waiter resolves and, since round four, the spared mark is deleted.
Result: the site is never listed as declined and never waits. The policy says it 'now has to wait before it can ask again ... unless another of its pages is asking to connect too: it's kept with the sites you declined'. Tab B was signing, not asking to connect. The policy says more is kept than is.
findings.who: Any connected site open in two tabs. No harm: less is kept than the policy says.
findings.evidence:
- dapp.ts:985-991 sharedBeyond: `… || this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin)`
- dapp.ts:792-795: `if (!this.spared.get(u.session.origin)?.question) this.spared.delete(u.session.origin);`
- Policy :29: '(a reload, say, unless another of its pages is asking to connect too)'
- Policy :93: the same exception.
- architecture.md:563 names both exceptions correctly ('or waits for the unlock itself').
- round4.json l3still#4 [left]: 'Whether the policy should name a page waiting for the unlock as sparing the site is a wording call for R4-docs.' 8b36053d didn't make it.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. I traced it on HEAD 1e1b0647 and confirmed it with a test in a copy, through DappService's real call(), unlocked(), gone(), stateChanged(), refuseFor() and declined() with the test fakes. The copy is deleted and the fix tree is clean.

**The trace (two tabs A and B of a site, wallet locked, both call signTx or signData)**
1. call() → run() → unlocked(): signTx and signData aren't in READ_METHODS (shared/dapp.ts:53-67), so each pushes an unlock waiter with `enable: false` and no countEnabling. `enabling` stays empty.
2. Tab A reloads. sw.ts:435 port.onDisconnect → gone(A). A's waiter is removed first, then dapp.ts:964 `if (!this.sharedBeyond(session)) this.refuseFor(...)`. sharedBeyond's dapp.ts:989 `this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin)` matches B's waiter (any method), so :966-970 sets `spared` with no `question`. refuseFor, the only writer of refusedUntil and keepRefusals, doesn't run.
3. The unlock. dapp.ts:795 `if (!this.spared.get(u.session.origin)?.question) this.spared.delete(u.session.origin);` drops the mark. After that, nothing lands it:
   - answer() refuses only a connect.
   - A signature left by its page isn't counted (dapp-gone.test.ts:406).
   - sparedNoMore (:1002) needs the leaving page in `enabling`.
4. The guards I checked all leave the site unrefused. If B leaves before the unlock, gone(B) takes :964 and refuses the site, but that's B's own leaving, which the policy's rule already covers. Closing the window refuses it too (:854-856). connectorOff clears everything.

**A twin the finder didn't name.** A's connect question waits through a lock (dapp-approvals-locked.test.ts), while B waits for the unlock to sign. Then A leaves.
- :989 spares the site, this time with `question: true`.
- A's enable() then unwinds, and call()'s finally → countEnabling, dapp.ts:621-623 `this.enabling.delete(session.origin); ... this.spared.delete(session.origin);`, drops the mark before any unlock.
- So the site is never refused here either.

**The docs.** Policy :29 says "unless another of its pages is asking to connect too", and :93 says the same with "it's kept with the sites you declined, in the browser's memory-only session storage". B is signing, not asking to connect, so the policy promises a refusal record that the code never writes. architecture.md:563 names the wider rule correctly ("or waits for the unlock itself"). privacy.md:350 has the policy's narrower wording word for word. flows.md:436 has it for a connect question.

**This is known and was left on purpose.**
- review3.json [3] checked_ok[5]: "the policy says more is kept than is, which is the safe side".
- round4.json policy_facts[3]: "naming it is a wording call". 8b36053d didn't make the change.

**Small corrections to the finding.**
- For the finder's connected site, "never listed as declined" doesn't tell the two cases apart: declined() leaves connected sites out whether refused or not (:1330 and its filter).
- What differs is the session-storage record and the wait. For a connected site the wait only matters while locked: its signatures are refused NOT_CONNECTED (:1658-1660).
- The policy gap predates round four. Round four only made the sparing permanent: before it, the mark lingered past the unlock (l3still#4).

**Why low, not medium.** The policy says more is kept, and more is refused, than the code does. Nothing extra is sent or kept. The back-off the policy promises is skipped only while another page of the same site holds the same unlock window open, and closing that window still refuses the site. The owner's B7 ("except when another page of the same site waits on that question") reads as covering another page waiting on the unlock window.
verdicts.fix_notes:
**Docs only.** Name the unlock wait in the exception, in the same words architecture.md:563 already uses.

1. **privacy-policy.md:29:** "(a reload, say, unless another of its pages is asking to connect too, or waiting for the unlock)".
2. **privacy-policy.md:93,** the 18 November entry, which is unshipped: "…unless another of its pages is asking to connect too, or is waiting for the unlock: it's kept with the sites you declined…".
3. **privacy.md:350,** the same sentence: add ", or waiting for the unlock" after "asking to connect too".
4. **flows.md:436,** the connect question: add "or is waiting for the unlock itself" beside "waiting on it or on its way to it". A connect question left while another page waits for the unlock to sign is spared too (the twin case).

Don't use the finder's "which then answers it":
- For a connect question left, the unlock answers nothing, yet the site is spared. The mark goes when the leaving page's enable() unwinds (dapp.ts:621-623), before any unlock.
- If the other page leaves before the unlock, the site is turned away for that page's own leaving (dapp.ts:964), which the general rule already says.

Nothing new is sent or kept, so there's no new Changes entry. The fix only corrects wording inside the unshipped 18 November entry.

**Sibling for the lead, outside this finding.** architecture.md:563 ends "and a connect question left stays owed (l3still#4)". That holds only when the sparing page is an enable() (the round-four pin, dapp-gone.test.ts:681). When the sparing page is a signature's unlock wait, nothing stays owed (the twin case).

Strictly, that twin also goes beyond the owner's B7 for a connect question: B waits on the unlock, not on A's question. A code change would be to have gone() count the :989 unlocking clause only for a page that left an unlock wait. There's no reachable harm today (the window is up for B anyway), so that's the lead's call, not this fix.

verdicts.evidence:
HOLDS on HEAD 1e1b0647. I traced the path end to end and found no guard.

**The path, from the press to the Koios request**
1. UI: `Lovejoin.tsx:1064` `anywayBox = status?.unsure?.[0] ?? status?.notMixed[0]`. `:1119-1121` turns that into `{ box, anyway: true }`, and `:3003-3008` sends it as `lovejoin-withdraw-now`. `handlers.ts:570-579` calls `withdrawNow(network, box, anyway, ...)`.
2. The `NotMixed` component offers the button whenever its count is above zero, and that count includes the unsure boxes (`sortOut :6323`, where unmixed = [..., ...deposits, ...unsure]).
3. `lovejoin.ts:7500` calls `ours()`, a pool read that asks nothing itself (`:3582-3625`). Then `:7523` `if (!anyway && !known(chosen)) force = [chosen];`: `anyway` only leaves `force` empty. `:7532` runs `sortOut` unconditionally.
4. `sortOut :6309` runs `rejudge` (on the device, no request), then `:6312` runs `found()`:
   - `:6487` unknown = boxes with no record and no kept origin.
   - `:6490-6493`, for every pool, retired ones included: all unknown boxes where `moreThanDue` holds, otherwise `theirs.filter((b) => s.asking?.[b.txHash] !== undefined)`.
   - `:6496` builds `ask`, and `:6498` calls `lookUp`.
5. `lookUp :6539-6545` → `madeBy :6582` → `inputsOf :6710-6714` `koiosAlone()` … `koios.txSpends(...)`. That is a tx_info request from the extension, so from the user's IP. Nothing on the path throttles it or skips a recently asked transaction.
6. `:6548-6554` keeps every silent transaction in `asking`. So an unsure box is always in `asking`: the box the button takes first is exactly one this press asks about.
7. Only after that: `:7536` skips the refusal for `anyway`, and `:7607` `withdrawOne` takes the box.

**The only escape**
A pool the data layer covers reads its provenance and sends nothing (`:6698-6706`). So the request is made only where Koios answers the pool: always on preprod; on mainnet with Koios-only on, with the data layer down, or for a later pool it doesn't cover. That is the finding's precondition.

**The test (Vitest, round-four WebAssembly)**
- (a) A plain restore: the press sends tx_info `[[N]]`.
- (b) A due time is left over, so `moreThanDue` is false at the press. It still sends `[[N]]`, through the `asking` branch alone.
  - No clause of the store policy lists this retry. A grep finds no "asked again" or "until it answers" about boxes. Only `privacy.md:475` mentions it, and the same sentence says Bring one back anyway doesn't ask.
- (c) Point 7: the retired run is marked done, and a classic (retired) pool box is in `asking`. It is free there (`waits`, `:6316`) and gets a due time (`scheduleFound :5785`). `withdrawDue`'s pool reads then ask `[[N],[N]]`, the second just before it comes back by itself. This contradicts `:28` ("a box comes back by itself from a retired pool without it") and `:93` ("nor before it comes back by itself from a retired pool").
- Control: a box whose answer is kept is taken with no request.
- The round-four fixer's note 3 (`round4.json`) said the anyway press's read "still follows the count rule". It doesn't: (b) is `:6492`'s `asking` branch.

**What holds for the policy**
These three ask nothing, so their clauses in `:28` and `:93` are true:
- Bring every box back now (`bringAllBackNow`, `:7718` on).
- The retired pools' run (`retireOnce`, `:4574`). Neither reaches `sortOut`, `found` or `made`. My first run of (c), without `retiredAlready`, passed because the retired run took N.
- Pay from my private balance anyway: `sessions.ts:2311` → `againBoxes(publicToo)`; `:3761` skips `made`; `split :7988` and `funding` do no lookup.

**Small imprecisions in the finding (verdict unchanged)**
- Point 6: `:44` at 51e66221 didn't say "before … bringing it back". That was main's shipped text. 51e66221's `:28` already said "a box you bring back yourself … comes back without that question". The exclusion started in round three, and round four kept it in its exact list.
- Point 5: `architecture.md:715`'s list of pool reads does include Bring one back now. It leaves out Bring one back anyway, a Bootstrap's Bring one back and the escape hatch, and its last sentence says Bring one back anyway doesn't ask.
- Point 4: N isn't in `moreThanDue`'s `held`. It counts as able to come back with no due time. The conclusion is the same.
- A sibling the finding missed: `architecture.md:152`, "one nobody asked about, as Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run and Bring one back anyway take them".

**Size of the leak**
It's a repeat of an ask Koios most likely already got, from the same IP, just before the withdraw. It is medium by the rubric (a request the policy says isn't made), but small in substance.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds at HEAD 1e1b0647. I traced it end to end and reproduced it in a scratch test.

**Trace**
1. The page sends `{box: unsure[0], anyway: true}` (`ui/screens/Lovejoin.tsx:1064` `anywayBox = (status?) => status?.unsure?.[0] ?? status?.notMixed[0]`; :1119-1122 `anywayRequest`; :3008).
2. `handlers.ts:570` passes it to `withdrawNow`.
3. In `withdrawNowNow`, `anyway` only skips `force` (`lovejoin.ts:7523` `if (!anyway && !known(chosen)) force = [chosen];`). `sortOut` still runs with no guard (:7532).
4. `sortOut` calls `found` (:6312). `found` takes every box in `asking` whatever the count says (:6492 `... ? theirs : theirs.filter((b) => s.asking?.[b.txHash] !== undefined)`), plus all unknown boxes where the count holds (:6496). It calls `lookUp` (:6498).
5. `lookUp` builds the Koios set for pools the data layer doesn't cover (:6544). `madeBy` → `inputsOf` → `koiosAlone().txSpends` (:6714) POSTs `tx_info`.
6. Only after that does `withdrawOne` take the box (:7607).
7. A box that `status` lists as `unsure` is by construction in `asking`, because `lookUp` writes `asking[tx] ??= at` for the silent ones (:6554).

**Repro**
Scratch test at `scratchpad/l4still1/anyway-asks.test.ts`, on the tree's fakes, no network:
- **(a) count holds.** M is mixed, N and P have no answer. `status` gives `unsure` [N, P] and `anywayBox` picks N. The anyway press then sends `tx_info` [[N, P]] and withdraws N#0, so it also groups P with N.
- **(b) count no longer holds** (one extra due time). The press sends `tx_info` [[N]]: the `asking` retry alone, which no item in the policy's list covers.
- **(c) control.** Bring every box back now (`bringAllBack` then `withdrawDue`) sends no `tx_info` and withdraws both boxes. That clause, Pay from my private balance anyway (`split`, no `sortOut`; `made` skipped for `publicToo`) and the retired pools' run (`bringAllBackNow`) all hold.
- **(d) step 7.** On a device that already ran the retired pools' run (`retired` set), a classic-pool box in `asking` is asked about in the same due run that then brings it back by itself: `withdrawDueNow`'s `sortOut` at :7276 runs before the `isRetired` skip at :7383.
- **(d2) after a restore**, `retireOnce` sends that box through `bringAllBackNow` with no request. So step 7 only happens on a device that already retired the pools and later finds a box there with no record, such as a 1.7 device's mix. It's narrower than the anyway case.

**Docs that say otherwise**
- `privacy-policy.md:28`: "**Bring one back anyway** … take a box without that question".
- `privacy-policy.md:93`: "never before … **Bring one back anyway** … takes it, nor before it comes back by itself from a retired pool". The same entry claims it says "exactly when" the wallet asks, yet :28, :44 and :93 never mention the retry.
- `privacy.md:475`: "Bring one back anyway takes does, since neither asks".
- `architecture.md:715`: "Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run and Bring one back anyway don't ask", and its list of pool reads leaves out the box-named and escape-hatch presses.

**Impact**
- **Who:** only the user, by an ordinary press. It needs a box Koios didn't answer for at the read that found it (a 429 on the public tier, or a lagging backend), and Koios answering that pool: preprod always; on mainnet, the Koios-only switch, the data layer down, or a later pool the data layer doesn't cover. After a restore, the button takes exactly that box first.
- **What they lose:** Koios gets one `tx_info` request from the user's IP naming that box's transaction, and every other unanswered one together, just before the withdraw. It is mostly a repeat: the first read most likely sent the same hashes, since a 429 is still a received request, and in Koios-only mode the withdraw goes to Koios as well. No money is at stake.
- **Severity:** medium, because the rubric names it: a request the policy says isn't made.

**Nothing later catches it**
- The words check `work/R4-docs/check_words4.py:53` and `:57` asserts the two wrong sentences are present.
- No test covers anyway on a box in `asking`. Round three's test (c) (review3.json l3time#1) used a box with a due time.
- R4-docs' note 3 reasoned from `force` and the count rule, and missed :6492's `asking` branch.
- The 18 November entry isn't on main (`grep -c` on main gives 0), so it's unshipped and can be fixed before release with no new date.

One small slip in the finding's step 6: it was main's :44 that said "before bringing it back or mixing it again". At 51e66221, :44 already said "before mixing it again or before it comes back by itself from one of Lovejoin's current pools". This doesn't change the verdict.

The finding holds on HEAD 1e1b0647. I traced the path end to end and found no guard the finder missed.

Path, Send: transfer.ts `build` -> `readContract` gives `utxos` (owned rows less reserved ones, Seedelf tokens, reference scripts and coin-control locks) and `classes` -> wasm `buildTransferParts` -> lib.rs:4960 first tries `build_transfer(sk, request.clone())` with every UTxO. Only a `too_much` error falls to parts. -> `transfer_spend` -> lib.rs:3396 `build::transfer_apart(.., &histories(Purpose::Pay, &request.classes)?, ..)` -> build.rs `select_script_inputs` -> `apart`. The `attempt` closure is `paying(..)?; spend.estimate()?`, whose `settle` refuses more than 22 inputs (10e9 steps / SPEND_BUDGET_GUESS 450M) as `TooMany`, which `try_with` maps to `Tried::Failed`.

Path, funding: sessions.ts `buildFunding` -> the same `readContract` -> `buildWithdrawParts` with `funding` -> `build_withdraw` -> lib.rs:3829 `Purpose::Fund` -> `sweep_many_apart` -> `apart`.

Classes: lovejoin.ts:8230-8236 classes a box the records don't place, a planted one, as `unplacedBox` (histories.ts: `box:<tx>+unknown:<tx>`, origin `lovejoin` by REACH) and a known-mixed box as `mixedBox` (origin `mixed`). The wasm `histories` (lib.rs:2158-2159) maps them to Origin::Lovejoin and Origin::Mixed. Both are tier 2 (build.rs:2546) and both are `is_box` (:2956).

Selection:
- build.rs:2958 `boxes.sort_by_key(|u| (!joins_base(u), std::cmp::Reverse(lovelace_of(u))));` has no rank.
- :2987-2993 builds `fewest_boxes` from `boxes[..j]`.
- Order a (:2936-2945, by rank) and order b (:2947-2955) put every tier-0 UTxO ahead of the boxes. So with 25 received payments of 2 ₳ and 43 ₳ paid out, both fail at k=23 on the limit before reaching any box.
- c with j=0 is a's prefix and is skipped (:3009-3013).
- c with j=1 is [largest box, the rest], which pays at 19 inputs.

Steps 1 and 2 don't catch it: every single UTxO is at or below `floor` and is Skipped, and each received payment is a class of its own.

Docs: round four's policy line (privacy-policy.md:93) says "A session's funding or a private payment, too, takes a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of", with no exception. architecture.md:137 says "(l3rank#3: no box someone else put in is picked over a mixed one on size)", while its own merge item 3 says "the j largest boxes". privacy.md:173 states the Send and funding orders without the exception too. flows.md:377 alone words the fallback correctly ("it tries other orders, spending as few boxes as pay"). round4.json's R4-code l3rank#3 "left" names this sibling and leaves it unchanged.

A wider precondition than the finder gave: a planted box is classed `unplacedBox` however it comes back, not only through Bring every box back now. It can also be made much larger than X by depositing into a pool of a larger box value. The harm window is set by X's size, though: amounts that 22 tier-0 UTxOs can't pay but X plus 21 of them can.

Severity: the code's harm alone is a narrow edge case. It needs 23 or more small tier-0 UTxOs, a planted box larger than a mixed one, and an amount in a window a few ₳ wide. But the harm is a privacy link made by default: a private Send or funding tied to S1 for anyone who reads its name, where the received payments tie it only to their payers. And the policy line is a claim wider than the code. The rubric rates both medium. If the owner accepts size order there and narrows the words, low fits.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Code fix (verified as a prototype in a copy of the tree, since deleted). The fix stays within the lead's rule ("a funding and a Send take a box a mix moved before a box of unknown making"), so it may not need the owner question.

1. build.rs, after :2958, add the same boxes ranked:
```rust
let mut ranked_boxes = boxes.clone();
ranked_boxes.sort_by_key(|u| (!joins_base(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)), std::cmp::Reverse(lovelace_of(u))));
```
For each j, `fewest_boxes` tries `ranked_boxes[..j]` with each of `rests` first, then `boxes[..j]` with each of `rests` where the two prefixes differ (`same`):
```rust
let (boxes, ranked_boxes, rests) = (&boxes, &ranked_boxes, &rests);
let fewest_boxes = (0..=boxes.len()).filter(|_| !largest.is_empty()).flat_map(move |j| {
    let mut picks: Vec<&[&UtxoResponse]> = vec![&ranked_boxes[..j]];
    if !same(&ranked_boxes[..j], &boxes[..j]) { picks.push(&boxes[..j]); }
    picks.into_iter().flat_map(move |chosen| rests.iter().map(move |others| (chosen.iter().chain(others.iter()).copied().collect(), j)))
});
```
This meets the fixer's objection: a mixed box too small to pay no longer pulls in a second box where the larger box pays alone, because the largest box is tried at the same j before j+1. Tier 2 holds only Mixed and Lovejoin, and every purpose ranks Mixed first (Pay 4<5, Fund 2<3, Mint 0<2). So "ranked prefix, then largest prefix" is complete for j=1: a smaller box of ADA alone can't pay where a larger one fails beside the same rest. It also covers Mint (the fixer's "Mint included"). At most it doubles c's orders, and `grown_before` still skips repeats.

Results with the prototype: the new failing test passes, the guard test passes, mint_test is 61/61, the whole seedelf-core suite is ok and seedelf-wasm --lib is 20/20.

2. Optional: give b's box tail the rank without touching b's tier-0 order. That is the key `(last, tier, !joins_base, if tier(u) == 2 { rank } else { 0 }, holds_tokens, Reverse(lovelace))`. b reaches boxes only after all tier-0 money, so this is rarely reached. Leave d (the CLI's order) as it is.

3. Docs once the code is fixed:
- architecture.md merge item 3: say "the j boxes the purpose ranks first (a box marked mixed before any other), then the j largest where they differ".
- Comment over c at build.rs:2922: say the same.
- The `Purpose::Pay` and `Purpose::Fund` doc comments, architecture.md:137's parenthetical and the policy line at :93 then hold as written.

If the owner accepts size order instead:
- Narrow policy :93, e.g. "...before one it can't tell the making of, unless it needs more of your UTxOs than one transaction can spend".
- Narrow architecture.md:137's parenthetical and privacy.md:173's Send and funding orders the same way.
- Leave flows.md:377 as it is.

4. Put both tests below in mint_test.rs `mod apart`, after a_stealth_mint_takes_a_mixed_box_before_one_of_unknown_making_whatever_the_sizes. They reuse `unplaced_and_mixed`, `funding`, `key_address`, `outpoints`, `one`, `BOX`. An end-to-end Vitest twin of mixed-box-before-unplaced.test.ts with 25 small received rows would need the wasm rebuild, so it's optional.

findings.owner_question: Should the stuck pool's note say that the wallet passes over a box tagged Unknown too?

verdicts.evidence:
I traced this on HEAD 1e1b0647 and the finding holds. There is no guard the finder missed. The gap is wider than the finding says.

1. How the way back is classed. A way back whose box's making the wallet can't place gets `unplacedBox = merged([boxFrom(w), unknownIn(w)])` (histories.ts:84). REACH (histories.ts:144) gives it origin "lovejoin". The UTxOs screen tags it ["Back from Lovejoin", "Unknown"] (histories.tag.lovejoin, en.json:773).

2. The payer order.
- lovejoin.ts:8146: `const fromLovejoin = (u: KoiosUtxo) => (knownBox(classes[outpoint(u)]) ? 0 : 1);`
- knownBox (histories.ts:219-220): `c?.origin === "mixed" || (c?.origin === "lovejoin" && parts(c).every((p) => p.startsWith("box:")))`. It is false for W.
- Next comes `another` (:8149). It is 0 for every UTxO when the box is no public account's.
- Then size (:8150-8152).
- withdraw_private_in (wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:2951-3010) then spends the first owned ADA-only UTxO that isn't PrivateTooSmall.
- Before round four this line was `["lovejoin","mixed"].includes(origin)`, so W went first. Round four changed only this line and its comment. round4.json l3time#3 "left": "stay true, so no string changes".

3. The words.
- en.json:1384: "Where it can, the wallet takes one that came back from Lovejoin." :1387 adds ", else one that ties no other account".
- es.json:1493/1496: "Siempre que puede, la billetera usa uno que haya vuelto de Lovejoin".
- ja.json:1275/1278: "可能な場合、ウォレットは Lovejoin から戻った UTxO を使います".
- PayerNotes (Lovejoin.tsx:1197) shows them in PaidQuestion (:1285), in AnywayQuestion when the pool is stuck (:1256) and in HeldQuestion when paying (:1532).
- The button builds, signs and sends (hatchRequest :1139 → withdrawOne). No review follows, so this note is all the user reads about which UTxO pays.

4. Reproduced end to end with the real WebAssembly.
- Mallory's 5 ₳ box goes in under S1's register and is brought back anyway. W lands at about 4.7 ₳ with class box:w+unknown:w.
- Beside it, 3 ₳ is recorded as a move-in, with class public:0.
- A stuck token box is brought back, paid privately. The 3 ₳ pays and W is not spent. The sealed way back's origin contains public:0.
- Without the 3 ₳, W pays the same box. So the wallet "can" take W.

5. Wider than the finder says.
- knownBox passes over every way back that carries a second tag: box+session, box+received, box+public:n and box+change. escape-hatch-unplaced-box.test.ts:196-198 pins this. My test shows knownBox is true exactly when historyTags is ["Back from Lovejoin"].
- box+public:n (tiedOrigin, PRIV-3) was passed over in 1.9.1 too (f265d178 lovejoin.ts:7602, `origin === "lovejoin"`).
- So the note has been loose since it was written. Three reviews accepted it, reading "came back from Lovejoin" as "Lovejoin alone". Round four makes W the newest case.
- Round four's own docs pass rewrote the same sentence. privacy.md:432 went from "One back from Lovejoin goes first" to "One back from Lovejoin with no other history goes first … not one whose making the wallet can't tell, tagged Unknown too", and flows.md:526 changed the same way. The note still says the old sentence.

6. Why low. The rubric puts a claim wider than the code at medium, but four things keep this one low:
- The sentence is a hedged preference.
- The first sentence of the note, that the payer and where it came from get tied to the box, stays true whichever UTxO pays.
- The code's pick is the owner's rule: W may tie whoever put it in, and a planted copy ties S1.
- It needs an ADA-only way back of unknown making that pays, no known box that pays, a smaller non-box UTxO and a stuck token pool.

Who: Mallory, with about 5 ₳ deposited under the user's Seedelf and brought back by hand. Or the user's own box, when it came back with nothing asked about its making (Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run). Either way the user's ordinary Bring one back on a stuck pool follows.
